author: salazarjosh
body:
# Overview
This pull request addresses two workflow-related issues in the CI/CD pipeline:

1. **Issue with multiple workflows running simultaneously on `master` merge:** Merging into `master` previously triggered multiple workflows simultaneously, overwhelming the database server and causing failures.
2. **Issue with Preview Workflow triggering multiple times on PR changes:** A new preview workflow would trigger with each change pushed to an open PR, potentially running more than one workflow simultaneously if rapid changes occurred.

#  Fixes

## Fix for Simultaneous Workflow Execution on Merge to Master
Staging Workflow now runs only if the Production Workflow was triggered on a merge to master AND completes successfully. This check is added to the end of the production deploy to trigger staging:
```
if: ${{ success() && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/master' }}
```

A new `on` trigger is added to the staging workflow to run on the `production_complete` event:
```
 repository_dispatch:
    types: [production_complete]
```

A similar check is added to the end of the staging deploy to trigger the backup workflow. This check also makes sure that THIS workflow was triggered from the `Production Workflow` event. This will prevent executing the backup workflow on any other automated workflow trigger for staging (a manual run, for example):
```
if: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_run' && github.workflow == 'Production Workflow' && github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' }}
```
and the backup workflow now runs on the `staging_complete` event:
```
 repository_dispatch:
    types: 
      - publish_production
      - staging_complete
```

This should trigger the workflows one at a time instead of all at once on merge to the master branch.

## Fix for Preview Workflow Running Multiple Times on PR Changes
Updated workflow to use `concurrency` to cancel any in progress workflow runs:
```
concurrency:
      group: previews-group
      cancel-in-progress: true
```

# Testing
- To test, we can merge this PR to master and see if the sequential deploys work.
- We can also publish two small changes in rapid succession to this branch to make sure the previous `previews` workflow cancels.

author: matthewfeickert
body:
Resolves #3371

**Use src directory layout**

* Move all package files under a non-importable src directory to validate packaging setup of the package for both full and editable installs.
   - c.f. https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/discussions/src-layout-vs-flat-layout/

**Update build system to use `src/` directory**

* Update the build system to use setuptools-scm to automatically determine version information from the version control system via dynamic versioning.
* Update setuptools build-backend to use src/ directory information for dynamically generated files.
* Remove packages find table given auotdiscovery of `src/` directory layout packages.
   - c.f. https://setuptools.pypa.io/en/latest/userguide/package_discovery.html#src-layout
* Remove `setuptools` `package-data` as in `pyproject.toml` based `setuptools` it is automatically included.
   - c.f. https://setuptools.pypa.io/en/latest/userguide/datafiles.html#include-package-data
* Remove the Git hash from the version information to have PEP 440 compliant version names.
   - c.f. https://peps.python.org/pep-0440/

**Remove use of `versioneer`**

* Remove versioneer related files:
   - Vendored `versioneer.py`.
   - versioneer specific `snakemake/_version.py`.
* Update `snakemake/__init__.py` to determine version information automatically from the generated `_version.py` file from `setuptools-scm`.

**Ignore `src/` directory dynamic files**

* Ignore `snakemake/assets/data` and `snakemake/_version.py` under the `src/` directory as these files are generated and shouldn't be versioned.

**Ensure sdist is only package and tests**

* Ensure the the sdist consists of the snakemake package, the tests in the tests directory, and relevant metadata files related to the project like the LICENSE. This is done by globally excluding all files and then including and grafting the files desired.

**Install snakemake to build docs**

* Snakemake needs to be importable to build the docs, and so as the 'snakemake' directory is no longer importable from the top level of the repository (intentionally) snakemake needs to be installed.

> [!NOTE] 
> In Issue https://github.com/snakemake/snakemake/issues/3371 I talked about avoiding the large diffs that come from something like this by using a `.git-blame-ignore-revs`. This needs to be done in a follow up PR, as it needs to know the commit hash to ignore, and as the PRs are squashed and merged the commit hash isn't known until after the PR has been merged in.

**Before submitting, make sure you've checked the following:**

- [x] **Prefix:** To cleary categorize this pull request, prefix the pull request title, using one of the following:
  - **BREAKING CHANGE**: Significant changes that may affect compatibility
  - **build**: Changes that affect the build system or external dependencies
  - **ci**: Changes to our continuous integration processes or workflows
  - **chore**: Refactor, cleanup, or other non-functional code changes
  - **docs**: Documentation update or addition
  - **feat**: Introduces a new feature or enhancement to the codebase
  - **fix**: Bug fix or error correction
  - **i18n**: Internationalization or localization changes
  - **perf**: Performance improvement
  - **refactor**: Code restructuring for better maintainability, readability, or scalability
  - **style**: Changes that do not affect the meaning of the code (white-space, formatting, missing semi-colons, etc.)
  - **test**: Adding missing tests or correcting existing tests
  - **WIP**: Work in progress, a temporary label for incomplete or ongoing work

# Changelog Entry

### Description

Introduced reactive statements that verify whether selected model supports:
- Web search
- Code execution
- Image generation

These are added as model capabilities to be specified on the ModelEditor. By default they will be true, so that the general admin setting 

### Added

- reactive capability statements:
  - Web search (`areSelectedModelsWebSearchCapable`)
  - Code execution (`areSelectedModelsCodeExecutionCapable`)
  - Image generation (`areSelectedModelsImageGenerationCapable`)
- capability text mapping for better UI readability
- helpTexts for the added capabilities

### Changed

- changed Tooltip for capabilities in the ModelEditor to use mapping

### Deprecated

No Deprecation

### Removed

Nothing removed

### Fixed

No fixes

### Security

No Security concerns

### Breaking Changes

- **BREAKING CHANGE**: The rendering of the capability UI element works in this direction: is it true in general settings? -> is it true in user settings? -> is it true in model capabilities?

The last check (is it true in model capabilities?) is added in this feature and by default true so that the default behavior is not altered.

---

### Additional Information

Linked Discussion: [11591](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/discussions/11591)

"My team and me discovered that it is currently not possible to specifically allow Web Search, Code Execution or Image Generation on model level.

This feature will be extremely helpful in my environment as we have a lot of on prem models that use highly sensitive data. We want the user to not be able to turn on these capabilities on these specific models, while keeping them on others.

Furthermore, it will be extremely helpful to adjust Image generation capabilities as some models are suited for the task and others are not (same for Code Execution) and therefore controlling if the user can access the capability on the model.

With this approach it will still be possible to give the user general access to all capabilities (Web Search, Code Execution, Image Generation) from the general settings, but also to specifically disallow the use on certain models."

### Screenshots or Videos

[Video Demo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f2835e5-1689-4dea-a859-5601a7800595)


### Documentation

No documentation of this feature was added yet. Will be done after PR is successfull.

### Dependencies

No new dependencies

### Testing

There is no testing implementation yet. If you got any advice on the setup of testing for this feature don't hesitate to comment below.

### Description
This PR implements the `ResetButtons` component, which provides the functionality to reset individual form fields or all fields at once. The component has been designed to be integrated into a larger form page (which will be handled separately), but it is ready to be used for resetting the specified fields.

### Changes
- **Feature:**
  - Created `ResetButtons` component to reset individual fields and reset all fields with user confirmation.

### How to Test
1. Use the `ResetButtons` component in a form by passing `fields` and `setFields` state as props.
2. Test the following scenarios:
   - **Reset Field**: Click the "Reset Field" button for each field. Ensure that only the respective field is cleared.
   - **Reset All**: Click the "Reset All" button and confirm the action. Ensure that all fields are cleared.

### Notes for Integration:
- The actual **form page** and **fields state** (`persona`, `context`, `task`, `output`, `constraint`) will be implemented in a separate task.
- This PR only covers the button functionality and provides the necessary logic for resetting fields. It should be integrated with the form page later where the form state will be managed.

### Key Components:

1. **Energy Production Contract**

1. Tracks energy generation from various sources
2. Includes producer registration and certification
3. Maintains verifiable production records
4. Tested for proper permissions and data integrity



2. **Consumption Monitoring Contract**

1. Records energy usage with consumer registration
2. Provides consumption verification mechanisms
3. Maintains usage history for transparency
4. Tested for access controls and data validation



3. **Peer-to-Peer Trading Contract**

1. Enables direct energy trading between users
2. Manages offers with pricing and expiration
3. Handles purchase transactions securely
4. Tested for market mechanics and edge cases



4. **Grid Balancing Contract**

1. Monitors grid stability across regions
2. Manages operator permissions by region
3. Records balancing actions for transparency
4. Tested for load calculations and stability metrics

Each contract includes comprehensive tests covering:

- Successful operations for all main functions
- Permission checks and access control
- Error handling for invalid inputs
- Edge cases for business logic
- Integration between contract components

- **Robust Permission Model**: Appropriate access controls for all state-changing functions
- **Comprehensive Querying**: Read-only functions for all important data points

author: njucjc
body:
When using the Accept header in HTTP requests, combining multiple content types into a single header rather than splitting them into multiple headers is recommended based on the following points:


- According to [RFC 7231](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7231#section-5.3.2), the Accept header field is used to specify the list of media types that the client can accept. The specification clearly states that these values should be separated by commas within a single header field.
` Accept = #( media-range [ accept-params ] )`

- In real-world development, sending multiple Accept headers can cause problems，Certain middleware or proxy servers might truncate or mishandle the request.

v2.0 Assembly snapshot - Customisable division specific metadata

Here we add functionality to allow for non-default metadata retrieval when creating release snapshots. 

-Added two new meta table query SQL files. One default (standard metadata as before) and one for plants (adding three new meta_keys: species.strain, strain.type and ploidy). 
- Also added species.common_name to both default and plants meta query sqls. 
- Tested and works fine in modenv setup. 
- Snapshot TSV generates much as before, with added meta cols. Taxonomy TSV generation unaffected. 
- Last change was to add species.strain_group (plants only) and species.display_name (default/plants)

author: austensen
body:
While we have postgis set up on our prod DB, it hasn't been incorporated into the wow code so when some nycdb datasets use postgis functions/types in their sql files it breaks our tests. This PR updates everything to solve this:
* the local dev setup now uses a postgis docker image
* creates the psotgis extension when initializing database connections used in the different testings suites
* updates our CircleCI docker images for the new versions (cimg/ instead of circleci) and using postgis

This also updates nycdb version in the python requirements to the current main branch, and updates some of the nycdb test data to reflect recent changes to datasets

author: mike-carey
body:
## Problem

<!-- What are you trying to solve? -->

We have flattened the org and are moving down to a single Developers team.

## Solution

<!-- How does this change fix the problem? -->

Removes the settings app.  Since it is not syncing branch protections, there is no point to it anymore.
Removes CODEOWNERship.  Since we are not using settings as code, we no longer need the protection.  Note that we can add this back as `* @shopsmart/developers` if we want all developers to be added to every PR.
Moves the PR template to the `.github` repository where it can be shared.  Any repo that wants to overwrite it can simply add their own.

## Notes

<!-- Additional notes here -->

- [x] Ruleset created and branch protection deleted
- [x] Wiki disabled, if applicable
- [x] Projects disabled
- [ ] Issues disabled, if applicable
- [x] Discussions disabled, if applicable
- [x] Always suggest updating branch

v    Before smashing the submit button please review the checkboxes.

☺ > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >  -->

## Description

The following PR allows client creators and the chain authority to optionally permission the V2 relaying on an IBC client along with UpdateClient

The configs are set **per** clientID in the v2 keeper and can be set by the creator or authority to a list of relayer addresses.

If the list is empty, this is interpreted as allowing permissionless relaying.

If the list is non-empty, only a relayer that matches an element in the list will be allowed to call `UpdateClient` and the v2 packet messages.

This is to ensure safety in the initial rollout of IBC v2. NOTE: All of the usual IBC client checks are still performed so we are not trusting the relayers for correctness.

We are trusting the relayers for liveness, and should there be an exploit in the new light clients being deployed with IBC V2; then we are trusting that these relayers will not exploit them. This is to ensure a safe and secure rollout for IBC V2.

We intend to remove this restriction and get back to permissionless relaying as the ecosystem gains confidence in the new protocol

body:
### Table Component The `Table` suite of components provides a set of customizable, accessible styled table primitives with BEM conventions. These components enable you to build data-rich tables that support responsive horizontal scrolling, default borders, and rounded corners. The API is flexible: you can override default styles using the `containerClassName` and `className` props for both light and dark themes. Notable improvements include a white theme hover effect, the use of `min-w-max` to prevent content stretching, the removal of extra top white space in the header, and support for a custom container classname. **Before:** ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0acaeb74-d9c9-477f-b68f-072e8bbaff0b) **After:** ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/19b38aae-ddf1-46b9-a4ee-c23d4b84e7b3) ### Props Below are the primary components and their relevant props. All components also accept standard HTML attributes (e.g. `className`, `onClick`, etc.) since they extend `HTMLAttributes` (or similar) under the hood. #### 1. `Table` - **containerClassName (optional)** - **Type**: `string` - **Description**: Custom class names applied to the outer container. Use this to override or extend border, rounded corners, and overflow styles. - **className (optional)** - **Type**: `string` - **Description**: Custom class names applied to the `` element, useful for overriding inner table styles like background color and text formatting. #### 2. `TableCaption` - **children (required)** - **Type**: `ReactNode` - **Description**: Caption text or content for the table. - **className (optional)** - **Type**: `string` - **Description**: Custom class names for the caption element. #### 3. `TableHeader` - **children (required)** - **Type**: `ReactNode` - **Description**: The header section of the table containing one or more header rows and cells. - **className (optional)** - **Type**: `string` - **Description**: Custom class names for the header section. #### 4. `TableBody` - **children (required)** - **Type**: `ReactNode` - **Description**: The body section of the table containing data rows and cells. - **className (optional)** - **Type**: `string` - **Description**: Custom class names for the body section. #### 5. `TableFooter` - **children (required)** - **Type**: `ReactNode` - **Description**: The footer section of the table, typically used for summaries or totals. - **className (optional)** - **Type**: `string` - **Description**: Custom class names for the footer section. #### 6. `TableHead` - **children (required)** - **Type**: `ReactNode` - **Description**: A header cell within a table header row. - **className (optional)** - **Type**: `string` - **Description**: Custom class names for header cells. #### 7. `TableRow` - **children (required)** - **Type**: `ReactNode` - **Description**: A row element that can contain header or data cells. The last row automatically removes its bottom border using the `last:border-0` utility. - **className (optional)** - **Type**: `string` - **Description**: Custom class names for the row element. #### 8. `TableCell` - **children (required)** - **Type**: `ReactNode` - **Description**: A data cell within a table row. - **className (optional)** - **Type**: `string` - **Description**: Custom class names for the cell element. ### Usage ```tsx 'use client'; import React from 'react'; import { Table, TableCaption, TableHeader, TableBody, TableFooter, TableHead, TableRow, TableCell, } from '@/components/common/Table'; export default function TableDemo() { return (

Motivation:
The core dependency was updated to OZ 4.9.0 a while ago. Now, it uses a contract only in 4.9.0, making it incompatible with 4.7.1 in this repo. Updating to 4.9.0 results in a breaking change to the TransparentUpgradeableProxy interface. These changes need to be addressed to maintain compatibility with the core protocol.

Modifications:
Updated TransparentUpgradeableProxy usage:
Modified imports to include ITransparentUpgradeableProxy alongside TransparentUpgradeableProxy
Updated proxy upgrade calls to cast to ITransparentUpgradeableProxy instead of TransparentUpgradeableProxy
Fixed ERC20Mock constructor errors:
Updated ERC20Mock in test files to use the new constructor pattern
Removed parameters from ERC20Mock constructor calls as the new version no longer accepts name, symbol, initialAccount, and initialBalance parameters

Result:
After these changes, middleware is compatible with the future EigenLayer core v1.3.0

author: mreishus
body: Fixes # ## Proposed changes: * **Expand the already-existing early exit in the `widget()` function to catch more cases of the [deprecated](https://twittercommunity.com/t/deprecating-widget-settings/102295) `data-widget-id` approach.** Twitter deprecated the use of `data-widget-id` around 2018, moving to a simpler approach using the href attribute with a valid Twitter username (e.g., `href="https://twitter.com/username"`). Our current code tries to detect the deprecated approach and bail early by looking for a `type=widget-id` variable. On an old site, I found an instance where `type` was not set, but `widget-id` was set to a large string of numbers. This seems to be another entry into the deprecated (now removed) code path. On the user's site, there are some messages in the JS console: ``` "You may have been affected by an update to settings in embedded timelines. See https://twittercommunity.com/t/deprecating-widget-settings/102295." "[Update] There have been recent updates to Embedded X Timelines and supported parameters..." ``` And the only thing that renders is a "My Tweets" link which is broken: This goes to a twitter.com/123456789012343456 URL, where the number is an unsuported "widget id". It leads to a "this account does not exist" page which tries to look up a username that is the exact long string of numbers. Here, I've moved the existing check to: ``` $explicit_widget_id = isset( $instance['type'] ) && 'widget-id' === $instance['type']; ``` And added a new check for: ``` $implicit_widget_id = empty( $instance['type'] ) && ! empty( $instance['widget-id'] ) && is_numeric( $instance['widget-id'] ); ``` Either one of them will now trigger the early exit. This looks to be safe since the new "happy path" way is setting `type=profile`. * **Only enqueue scripts when needed** The twitter JS is heavy and downloads and parses a lot of code. Instead of always enqueuing it on class construction when the widget is active, it is now letting the `widget()` function enque it after it passes the deprecated settings check. This way, sites with misconfigured settings won't queue up a large amount of JS that will ultimately do nothing. ### Other information: - [ ] Have you written new tests for your changes, if applicable? - [ ] Have you checked the E2E test CI results, and verified that your changes do not break them? - [ ] Have you tested your changes on WordPress.com, if applicable (if so, you'll see a generated comment below with a script to run)? ## Jetpack product discussion ## Does this pull request change what data or activity we track or use? ## Testing instructions: ### Broken site * On WPCOM, sandbox and visit this site on trunk: 373a5-pb/#plain * Open the sidebar using the hamburger menu, find the "My Tweets" link and confirmed it's broken * See the error messages about twitter deprecation in the console * Use the debug bar to confirm the twitter timeline js was enqueued * Apply the patch * Reload the site * Error messages in console should be gone * Confirm using the debug bar that the twitter timeline js is no longer enqueued * Now there should be an error message about incorrect settings visible to admins instead of the broken "My Tweets" link ### Working site For a site where the twitter timeline is working before this patch, it should continue to work after the patch and not trigger any new errors. In order to set up a site, I had to unhide this: ``` diff --git a/wp-content/mu-plugins/jetpack-plugin/sun/modules/widgets/twitter-timeline.php b/wp-content/mu-plugins/jetpack-plugin/sun/modules/widgets/twitter-timeline.php index d6769bfbb39..b6349bfb6d7 100644 --- a/wp-content/mu-plugins/jetpack-plugin/sun/modules/widgets/twitter-timeline.php +++ b/wp-content/mu-plugins/jetpack-plugin/sun/modules/widgets/twitter-timeline.php @@ -48,7 +48,7 @@ class Jetpack_Twitter_Timeline_Widget extends WP_Widget { } add_action( 'admin_enqueue_scripts', array( $this, 'admin_scripts' ) ); - add_filter( 'widget_types_to_hide_from_legacy_widget_block', array( $this, 'hide_widget_in_block_editor' ) ); + /* add_filter( 'widget_types_to_hide_from_legacy_widget_block', array( $this, 'hide_widget_in_block_editor' ) ); */ } /** ``` Then go to wp-admin/widgets.php, add a legacy widget, and inside there, add a Twitter Timeline widget. Sadly, even with the updated username format all this does is create a link to the page.. However, the patch doesn't break this and is an improvement for sites without usernames.

author: irby
body:
This change set fixes an issue where the access token generated by using ambient credentials with GCP is not compatible with Command. The current code generates only an opaque access token, however Command requires the token be in JWT format.

Google's OAuth SDK does not expose a way to generate an OAuth access token in JWT format. Instead, the only way to produce a valid JWT signed by Google's OAuth server is by producing an ID token. The idtoken flow requires an audience. So, I've introduced a config value for `audience` that can be optionally set by the end user -- if not set, it will default the `aud` claim to `command`.

Because we are using an OIDC ID token instead of an OAuth access token, there are slight differences in the JWT produced. For example, the `scopes` provided will not appear in the JWT. However, end users can configure their Command instance to validate claims such as `aud` and `email` to assign identities to roles.

author: ludovicm67
body:
Fixes #265.

## Before the change

Note that if you clone the repo using SSH, the `sed` substitution is not working.
But it is working as expected for HTTP.

### Using SSH

```sh
> echo "git@github.com:Azure/azure-saas.git" | sed 's/.*\/\([^ ]*\/[^.]*\).*/\1/'

git@github.com:Azure/azure-saas.git
```

### Using HTTP

```sh
> echo "https://github.com/Azure/azure-saas.git" | sed 's/.*\/\([^ ]*\/[^.]*\).*/\1/'

Azure/azure-saas
```

## With this change

Note that the result with HTTP doesn't change, and that now the results with SSH is the same as with HTTP.

### Using SSH

```sh
> echo "git@github.com:Azure/azure-saas.git" | sed 's/.*\/\([^ ]*\/[^.]*\).*/\1/' | sed 's/.*:\(.*\)\.git/\1/'

Azure/azure-saas
```

### Using HTTP

```sh
> echo "https://github.com/Azure/azure-saas.git" | sed 's/.*\/\([^ ]*\/[^.]*\).*/\1/' | sed 's/.*:\(.*\)\.git/\1/'

Azure/azure-saas
```

## Conclusion

This second `sed` command has no effect on HTTP urls, as it just removes the content that is before the `:` and the trailing `.git`, but it ensures that if the repo was cloned using SSH, the value of `git_org_project_name` will be the same as it was cloned using HTTP.

This solves the issue #265.

exten=> _1.,1,SayAlpha(${EXTEN})

## **Description**

Adds support for `metamask_accountChanged` notification via `wallet_notify` ([CAIP-319](https://github.com/ChainAgnostic/CAIPs/blob/main/CAIPs/caip-319.md)) notification to enable our wallet-standard implementation to forward account changed events via the [wallet standard change event](https://github.com/wallet-standard/wallet-standard/blob/c6fa5fd7d58e9ea1e6762127d16585fbb56ff88a/packages/core/features/src/events.ts#L84)

This is not a pattern we want to continue since the Multichain API should not require account changing. This is a one off bespoke implementation to support a Solana wallet-standard interface.

[![Open in GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)](https://codespaces.new/MetaMask/metamask-extension/pull/30949?quickstart=1)

E2E testing for this feature should be handled in the Wallet Standard powered test dapp one we have it cc @EdouardBougon @baptiste-marchand 

## Demo video

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d5234fe-824d-4d43-9571-8178e220ad35



## **Related issues**

Fixes: https://github.com/MetaMask/MetaMask-planning/issues/4193

## **Manual testing steps**
0. Build in flask
1. Generate 2 Solana Accounts
2. Go to any site
3. Open the dev console and run the following script:
```
const extensionPort = chrome.runtime.connect(<your extension id>)

extensionPort.onMessage.addListener((msg) => {
  console.log(msg.data)
})

extensionPort.postMessage({
  type: "caip-x",
  data: {
    jsonrpc: "2.0",
    method: "wallet_createSession",
    params: {
      requiredScopes: {},
      optionalScopes: {
        "solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp": {
          methods: ["getAccount"],
          notifications: [],
          accounts: ['solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp:<SOLANA_ACCOUNT_ADDRESS_1>',
          'solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp:<SOLANA_ACCOUNT_ADDRESS_2>']
        }
      },
  sessionProperties: {'solana_accountChanged_notifications': true},
};,
  }
})

```
4. Switch between the two Solana accounts in the account selector in the wallet UI
5. You should see console logs in the dev console:
```
{
    "method": "wallet_notify",
    "params": {
        "scope": "solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp",
        "notification": {
            "method": "solana_accountChanged",
            "params": "<YOUR_SOLANA_WALLET_ADDRESS>"
        }
    }
}
```

author: mineo333
body:
The following PR addresses #26510 

I've spent some time looking into this and it seems to be a limitation of the Mach-O format based on compiler/linker code. 

Looking in the LLVM source code, whenever we have a difference between two symbols it hits `ARMMachObjectWriter::recordARMScatteredRelocation`. The call for this can be found [here](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/52fc6ffcda0895c0c7b976ad1f5cb5a282b571d2/llvm/lib/Target/ARM/MCTargetDesc/ARMMachObjectWriter.cpp#L375). In `ARMMachObjectWriter::recordARMScatteredRelocation`, we get the address associated with both symbols and we create a `ARM_RELOC_SECTDIFF` entry that the mach-o linker will relocate. The subtraction expression error can also be found [here](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/52fc6ffcda0895c0c7b976ad1f5cb5a282b571d2/llvm/lib/Target/ARM/MCTargetDesc/ARMMachObjectWriter.cpp#L279). 

Now, interestingly, according to some [comments](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/cctools/blob/3406a8e0f9ec28862967217797fe2b9a7b3d10ed/ld/arm_reloc.c#L1381) in apple's `ld`, we see that  `ARM_RELOC_SECTDIFF` are always scattered. 

Looking at some more [code](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/cctools/blob/main/include/mach-o/reloc.h#L151) in apple's compiler code, we see that a scattered relocation entry has value instead of a symbol index. So, it seems we need to always have concrete values instead of undefined symbols. 

TL;DR, the Mach-O format for ARMv7 has a key limitation where it seems it cannot use undefined symbols in a subtraction due to how its relocations function. 

We also cannot introduce a simple extern symbol as the linker also rejects that.

It seems, after some investigation using clang's `-S` feature, the proper way to do something like this is to introduce the symbol into an `__nl_symbol_ptr` section and use a relative addressing scheme to get the value of the symbol pointer.  

This PR introduces apple-specific code to put the `OPENSSL_armcap_P` in a `__nl_symbol_ptr` section instead of putting it in the `.text` section. 

Tagging: @bbbrumley 
Tagging: @cjf7669

author: michaelmilstead
body:
Previously during the first streamed message was fetching the remote thread during switching the local currentThreadId, which would sometimes return an "older" thread state than was currently available through returned chunks.

Fixes that by switching the thread without fetching, and fetching the remote thread for final state after chunks complete.

author: jakemer
body:
The `form-control-monetary` field has only been used in the payment provisioning form so far, where amounts are submitted as whole numbers (dollars).

Elsewhere (within our Payments system), amounts are submitted in the smallest currency denomination (cents) and need to be formatted differently.

Example:
In the provisioning form: user inputs "1,000", which gets submitted as "1000" (dollars)
In other places (such as the refund component in this PR): user inputs "1,000.00" which gets submitted as "100000" (cents)

We had been using `imask` for the `form-control-monetary` before, which really does not play nicely with the with the second example. Fortunately, achieving the behavior we want isn't too difficult to do manually.

Changes:
- Move `form-control-monetary` to the provisioning component directory and rename it to `form-control-monetary-provisioning` to prevent confusion. It should only be used here anyhow.
- Make a new component named `form-control-monetary` to act as our primary currency input (cents shown as decimal dollar value)
- Internally manage form vs display values in that component
- Refactor `formatCurrency` helper to also work for the new input (omit the currency symbol) so that the code is shared and consistent
- Test the `formatCurrency` helper changes to ensure no regressions

Developer considerations
--------------

- On any task
  - [ ] Previous unit and e2e tests are passing
  - [ ] Perform dev QA on Chrome, Firefox, and Safari
- On new features
  - [ ] Add unit tests
  - [ ] Add e2e tests
  - [ ] Add documentation
  - [ ] Does the component have exportedparts for styling? If so, add unit a unit test for each exportedpart
- On bugs
  - [ ] Add unit tests to prevent the bug from happening again


Developer QA steps
--------------------

New monetary input:
- [x] Pull this branch and run `pnpm install`
- [x] Run `pnpm dev:refund-payment`, and go to `localhost:3420`
- [x] The amount field should default to the value passed in the `refund-payment.js` file (`payment-amount-refundable` prop)
- [x] In the "amount" field, try entering different values and characters. Only numbers should be accepted, and the numbers should be formatted as expected (thousands separator and two decimal places, for example 1,234.56)
- [x] Trigger validation. Any entered value that exceeds the `payment-amount-refundable` should throw an error saying that it cannot exceed that amount (`$10.00`)
- [x] The submit button text should update to the entered amount saying "Refund $x.yz"

Provisioning monetary input:
- [x] Run `pnpm dev:payment-provisioning`
- [x] Proceed through the form until you arrive at "Additional Questions" and enter some values into the `$` fields. These fields should not display any decimals, but should still have commas as thousand separators

author: daisieh
body:
Federation needs to check for candig authorization itself and only send the fanout call to other federation nodes if candig-authzed locally.
If a federation node gets a call from another server's fanout call, we know that it's from a candig-authzed user on that node, so federation can add its service token before sending the call to its locally-registered services.

I also consolidated the local get_service/post_service call into a single send_service_request call because it was basically the same code, slowly diverging. Also having FederationResponse.get_service and operations.get_service that do two different things is confusing.

author: corngood
body:
For update scripts we pipe stderr to stdout, since this appears to be simpler than vice-versa.  CalledProcessError now includes stdout.

merge_changes is moved out of the try: block.  This will result in a behaviour change.  Errors in merging will end ignore keep-going, and errors will bypass the update-script log handling.

This helps for tools which use stdout heavily for diagnostics (e.g. dotnet/msbuild).

It still requires caching everything in memory, but avoiding that would require temporary files.

We could also keep separate log files for stdout/err, but interleaving them is usually more useful IMO.

1. Install the `express-rate-limit` package.
2. Import the `express-rate-limit` package in the `server/vite.ts` file.
3. Set up a rate limiter with appropriate configuration (e.g., maximum of 100 requests per 15 minutes).

author: bdieterm
body:
Before this PR there was the danger of data loss after reloading:
User adds changes to a file and saves it (and keeps the file open in the Pyzo editor).
An external program rewrites the file.
The user switches focus in Pyzo and gets the "File was changed" dialog.
User presses "Keep this version".
User closes Pyzo. Changes are lost because Pyzo does not even ask to save the version in the editor.
With this PR, when pressing "Keep this version" the document in the editor is marked as modified.

Pyzo does a file modification check as well when the user saves the file (e.g. via Ctrl+S).
Before this PR, the check displayed a message box with choices "Keep this version" and "Reload". In my opinion, "Reload" is a bit out of place when saving a file.
With this PR, the check while saving gets its own dialog with choices "Cancel saving" and "Overwrite file".

When checking for external changes to a loaded file, indicated via the file modification metadata of the filesystem, the originally loaded/saved data from the Pyzo editor will be compared to the new data in the file. If the contents are equal, the file is considered unmodified. The Pyzo editor keeps the whole original binary data in memory for that comparison when loading and saving a file.

If a file that is opened with unsaved changes in the Pyzo editor was changed on the storage, Pyzo will ask to either "Keep this version" or to "Reload".
But if the opened file has no unsaved changes (white symbol instead of red symbol with floppy disk), Pyzo will now also give the third choice "Always reload". When clicking that button, the "auto reload" feature will be activated, and the user gets informed about that auto-reload feature and how to disable it again (in the "Advanced settings" dialog). The auto-reload feature will automatically reload files that are not marked as modified in the Pyzo editor instead of asking the user.

A use case for auto reloading is when having the same files open in Pyzo and another editor application, as mentioned in #1155. Auto reloading might also be useful when switching branches in git, for example.

Cherry-picked git: Hard wrap in editor  (#26507)

This adds the ability for the editor to implement hard wrap (similar to
"textwidth" in vim).

If you are typing and your line extends beyond the limit, a newline is
inserted before the most recent space on the line. If you are otherwise
editing the line, pasting, etc. then you will need to manually rewrap.

Release Notes:

- git: Commit messages are now wrapped "as you type" to 72 characters.

# What does this implement/fix?

Add preset modes to Tuya Fan, matching how other fan types support it.

Review notes: This required calling publish_state() on control() which Tuya components usually don't do (or do more directly through their uart communication).  But it is needed to hook into callbacks for things like `on_preset_set`.  I wasn't sure if there was a better way to do this, as I'm not sure calling the callback directly is exposed.  Let me know if this needs adjustment.  It appears to work fine on my fan switch.  I set all other states in control() just to be safe to make sure things don't get out of sync.  Uart should still be triggering everything the same as it always has.

This PR implements a new feature that provides units with more intuitive, natural language descriptions of their surroundings to help the LLM make better decisions during gameplay. Key additions include:

1. A new `get_relative_direction` helper function that calculates the relative direction between positions on the map (e.g., "up-left", "down-right").

2. A comprehensive `get_unit_surroundings` function that generates human-friendly descriptions of:
   - Nearby coins with precise directions and distances (e.g., "3 steps away up-right (1 step up and 2 steps right)")
   - Water obstacles within a 3-step radius
   - Other units and their relative positions
   - Map boundaries when the unit is at an edge

3. Updated the `get_unit_move_decision` function to include these descriptions in the prompt to the LLM.

This enhancement should help the LLM navigate more effectively as it now has a clearer understanding of the game state in natural language, rather than having to interpret the raw coordinates and map.

Closes #35

author: torrancew
body:
This commit introduces real-time load statistics (in Watts) and lifetime energy statistics (in Wh) for the Franklin Smart Circuits and V2L

Note that my installation does not have V2L enabled and so, while I've attempted to make sure they're supported, they are completely untested.

There are still some open questions here around what other possible states may exist -- my installation has a single logical Smart Circuit which is hooked up across what the software reports as Switch 1 and Switch 2. I have an unused slot in my Franklin App labelled Switch 3, but don't see any statistics for it, and assume it's somehow tangled up in the V2L data that's reported.

Once we get this to a place we're happy with, and get it released to PyPI, we can [update the HA integration](https://github.com/richo/homeassistant-franklinwh/issues/27) to depend on this version and expose the data as sensors there.

Example output:

```
In [4]: client.get_stats()
Out[4]: Stats(current=Current(solar_production=0.275, generator_production=0, battery_use=-0.032, grid_use=1.709, home_load=1.952, battery_soc=19.368, switch_1_load=612, switch_2_load=624, v2l_use=0), totals=Totals(battery_charge=0.17, battery_discharge=2.898, grid_import=12.682, grid_export=0.04, solar=1.79, generator=0, home_use=17.16, switch_1_use=37246, switch_2_use=37458, v2l_export=212, v2l_import=54))
```

I can confirm that the stats reported here are logically consistent with what I see in the app for my own install, though it's clear that the reporting is inconsistent with the rest of the Franklin ecosystem. Given that that's how upstream is handing it to us, I'm inclined to keep it that way for now.

author: joerunde
body:
Quick fix for a small bug with the log introduced in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/14466

That warning log always prints, since we actually configure the v1 scheduler as a string. 🤦 

This change instead checks the resolved class, using an equality check against the existing V1 scheduler class. I did it this way, instead of `isinstance(scheduler, V1Scheduler)`, since existing scheduler classes may inherit from the V1 scheduler and we still want to print the warning if that's the case.

author: ericstj
body:
We weren't handling EXEs correctly - simply missed this case.

When a global.json mentions a version that doesn't exist on the path, the `dotnet --version` command will fail, and the `commandLineInvocationService` will throw InvalidOperationException since it cannot distinguish this failure from a missing command.  Catch this exception and treat it like a failure so we fallback to parsing `global.json`.

author: taizun-jj202
body:
Added Function to detect launch using X,Y,Z accleration.

Acceleration  = sqrt( 
                                (accX * accX) * 
                                (accY * accY) * 
                                (accZ * accZ) );

If this value is above (greater than) `LAUNCH_DETECT` threshold in G or `LAUNCH_DETECT_mps` (meters per second) value that is globally defined in `launch_detect.c` file, then `true` is returned else `false` is returned.

author: ajtmccarty
body:
IFC-1375

adds the DataLoader pattern to the many_relationships_resolver to reduce the number of database calls. if a many relationship includes a `limit` or `offset`, we need to fall back to the old way of retrieving cardinality-many relationships (at least one query for each node) b/c the offsets and limits will not work correctly when multiple nodes are batched together

I've captured more performance improvement ideas in IFC-1382

author: mdhaber
body:
#### Reference issue
Toward gh-14651, gh-20544 
Together with the new `vectorized_filter` (gh-22575), this makes gh-9873 much easier.

#### What does this implement/fix?
`scipy.stats.mode` natively works only with 1-D slices; the `_axis_nan_policy` decorator loops over slices to add `axis` support. This PR replaces the implementation with one that is natively vectorized.

#### Additional information
The upside is ~90x speed improvement in cases where we have many short slices; the downside is 2x slowdown when we have a few long slices.

```python3
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

rng = np.random.default_rng(23458924958234563)

# times are:
# main
# PR

x = rng.integers(0, 10, size=1_000_000)
# %timeit stats.mode(x)
# 5.53 ms ± 208 μs per loop (mean ± std. dev. of 7 runs, 100 loops each)
# 11.6 ms ± 137 μs per loop (mean ± std. dev. of 7 runs, 100 loops each)

y = x.reshape(100, 10000)
# %timeit stats.mode(y, axis=-1)
# 8.61 ms ± 24 μs per loop (mean ± std. dev. of 7 runs, 100 loops each)
# 16 ms ± 1.54 ms per loop (mean ± std. dev. of 7 runs, 100 loops each)

y = x.reshape(10000, 100)
# %timeit stats.mode(y, axis=-1)
# 333 ms ± 3.34 ms per loop (mean ± std. dev. of 7 runs, 1 loop each)
# 18.6 ms ± 164 μs per loop (mean ± std. dev. of 7 runs, 100 loops each)

y = x.reshape(100000, 10)
# %timeit stats.mode(y, axis=-1)
# 3.33 s ± 38.2 ms per loop (mean ± std. dev. of 7 runs, 1 loop each)
# 36.8 ms ± 320 μs per loop (mean ± std. dev. of 7 runs, 10 loops each)
```

It would be simple to use the old implementation when the input is 1-D.
As an enhancement, we could also add a heuristic to loop when looping is expected to be faster.

body:
This PR adds 4 new rules:
- Present in amount of other collections (incl. smart collections)
- Present in amount of other collections (incl. parents and smart collections)
- [list] Collections media is present in (titles) (incl. parents and smart collections)
- [list] Collections media is present in (titles) (incl. smart collections)

These use the same logic as the existing non-smart collection rules, with the addition of checking smart collections.

Smart collections are not returned in the metadata Collection array. Instead we must iterate over each smart collection, load its children and then check if the rating key is present.

The rule IDs skip a few to cater for the ones added in PR #1627

author: stephenquan
body: On iOS / maccatalyst custom fonts do not react to FontAttributes such as Bold and Italic. See https://github.com/dotnet/maui/issues/7574. Instead, one has to change FontFamily to achieve the same result. To help with this, I introduced a FontMap class which has a Dictionary that replaces problematic FontFamily, FontAttributes tuples with working FontFamily, FontAttributes.

author: owenkephart
body:
## Summary & Motivation

This makes a few changes to how implicit Definitions loading works.

In particular, defs files can now be located at any level of the hierarchy, including the top level. Previously, definitions files at the top level of the `defs/` directory would be ignored.

Conceptually, this lets the system distinguish between two types of "implicit definitions loading":

1. cases where the user has explicitly created a `Definitions` object to organize their definitions.
2. cases where users are defining bare python objects in files

This PR does this distinction by:

1. if there is a `component.yaml` file in the directory, then the entire directory (and all subdirs) are handled by that component's logic.
2. if there is a `component.py` file in the directory, then the entire directory (and all subdirs) are handled by that component's logic
3. if there is a `definitions.py` file in the directory, then the entire directory is handled by a single DefinitionsComponent. If that component finds a `Definitions` object in the directory, that will be used, otherwise all files will be scanned (recursively) to  find and load any dagster definitions found therein.
4. if none of the above are true, a unique DefinitionsComponent is created for each individual python file in the directory. This will load any dagster definitions found in that file.

Some situations to consider:

## Scenario 1

`assets.py` contains standalone `@asset`s

```
defs/
  some_component/
    component.yaml
  assets.py
```

Here, the idea is to automatically load all defs in `assets.py`.

## Scenario 2

`assets.py` contains standalone `@asset`s that are imported in `definitions.py`

```
defs/
  some_component/
    component.yaml
  assets.py
  definitions.py
```

Here, we notice that `definitions.py` has a `Definitions` object, and avoid re-loading the assets in `assets.py`.

## Scenario 3

`assets.py` contains standalone `@asset`s that are imported in `definitions.py`

```
defs/
  some_component/
    component.yaml
  team_a_defs/
    assets/
      assets.py
    definitions.py
```

Here, we notice that `definitions.py` has a `Definitions` object, and avoid re-loading the assets in `assets.py`.

author: jrfnl
body:
# Description
As things were, a ruleset loading an invalid sniff - a sniff which doesn't implement the `Sniff` interface and is missing either the `register()` or `process()` method, or both -, would result in fatal errors which are unfriendly to the end-user.

Now, while this will hopefully be a very rare occurrence and should no longer be possible as of PHPCS 4.0, which intends to remove support for sniffs not implementing the `Sniff` interface, I still believe it prudent to show more user-friendly and more informative error messages to the end-user until that time.

This commit implements this and executes step 2 to address issue #694.

Includes tests.

Output of commands involving various invalid sniffs **before** this PR:

```
$ phpcs -ps . --standard=./tests/Core/Ruleset/RegisterSniffsRejectsInvalidSniffNoImplementsNoRegisterTest.xml

Fatal error: Uncaught Error: Call to undefined method TestStandard\Sniffs\InvalidSniffError\NoImplementsNoRegisterSniff::register() in path/to/PHP_CodeSniffer/src/Ruleset.php:1505
Stack trace:
  thrown in path/to/PHP_CodeSniffer/src/Ruleset.php on line 1505
```

```
$ phpcs -ps . --standard=./tests/Core/Ruleset/RegisterSniffsRejectsInvalidSniffNoImplementsNoProcessTest.xml

PHP_CodeSniffer version 3.11.1 (stable) by Squiz and PHPCSStandards

Fatal error: Uncaught Error: Call to undefined method TestStandard\Sniffs\InvalidSniffError\NoImplementsNoProcessSniff::process() in path/to/PHP_CodeSniffer/src/Files/File.php:519
Stack trace:
  thrown in path/to/PHP_CodeSniffer/src/Files/File.php on line 519
```

```
$ phpcs -ps . --standard=./tests/Core/Ruleset/RegisterSniffsRejectsInvalidSniffNoImplementsNoRegisterOrProcessTest.xml

PHP_CodeSniffer version 3.11.1 (stable) by Squiz and PHPCSStandards

Fatal error: Uncaught Error: Call to undefined method TestStandard\Sniffs\InvalidSniffError\NoImplementsNoRegisterOrProcessSniff::register() in path/to/PHP_CodeSniffer/src/Ruleset.php:1505
Stack trace:
  thrown in path/to/PHP_CodeSniffer/src/Ruleset.php on line 1505
```

Output of commands involving various invalid sniffs **after** this PR:
```
$ phpcs -ps . --standard=./tests/Core/Ruleset/RegisterSniffsRejectsInvalidSniffNoImplementsNoRegisterTest.xml

ERROR: Sniff class TestStandard\Sniffs\InvalidSniffError\NoImplementsNoRegisterSniff is missing required method register().
```

```
$ phpcs -ps . --standard=./tests/Core/Ruleset/RegisterSniffsRejectsInvalidSniffNoImplementsNoProcessTest.xml

ERROR: Sniff class TestStandard\Sniffs\InvalidSniffError\NoImplementsNoProcessSniff is missing required method process().
```

```
$ phpcs -ps . --standard=./tests/Core/Ruleset/RegisterSniffsRejectsInvalidSniffNoImplementsNoRegisterOrProcessTest.xml

ERROR: Sniff class TestStandard\Sniffs\InvalidSniffError\NoImplementsNoRegisterOrProcessSniff is missing required method register().
ERROR: Sniff class TestStandard\Sniffs\InvalidSniffError\NoImplementsNoRegisterOrProcessSniff is missing required method process().
```


## Suggested changelog entry
The user will be shown an informative error message for sniffs are missing one of the required methods.
Previously this would result in a fatal error.

body:
<!-- What issue does this PR close? -->
Closes #5407

<!-- What does this PR achieve? [feature|hotfix|fix|refactor] -->

Updates carousels such that new cards are rendered server-side.

The main `/partials` handler has been updated to handle requests for `_component` `CarouselLoadMore`.  When such requests are made, one of four search queries are executed and an array of carousel card HTML is returned in the response.

The search query that is used is determined by the `queryType` search parameter:

| `queryType` | Search Used | Where Used |
|---|---|---|
| `SEARCH` | [`work_search`](https://github.com/internetarchive/openlibrary/blob/cb5628dbb5d69b834e42e91dd24857662c0875bf/openlibrary/plugins/worksearch/code.py#L788) | QueryCarousels |
| `BROWSE` | archive.org search via [`get_available`](https://github.com/internetarchive/openlibrary/blob/cb5628dbb5d69b834e42e91dd24857662c0875bf/openlibrary/core/lending.py#L238) | Several homepage `custom_ia_carousel` calls |
| `TRENDING` | [`get_trending_books`](https://github.com/internetarchive/openlibrary/blob/cb5628dbb5d69b834e42e91dd24857662c0875bf/openlibrary/views/loanstats.py#L54) | Homepage trending `custom_carousel` call |
| `SUBJECTS` | [`get_subject`](https://github.com/internetarchive/openlibrary/blob/cb5628dbb5d69b834e42e91dd24857662c0875bf/openlibrary/plugins/worksearch/subjects.py#L155) | Used by subject and publisher page `custom_carousel` calls |

Contributes to https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/1541 Structs cannot be passed around in async code (a copy gets created), we need to convert them to classes so they can be used in the incoming async code. Here's the perf impact comparison before and after: | Method | Toolchain | Mean | Error | StdDev | Median | Min | Max | Ratio | RatioSD | Allocated | Alloc Ratio | |-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-| | ZipFileCreateFromDirectory | Before
(struct) | 11.16 ms | 0.485 ms | 0.558 ms | 11.13 ms | 10.05 ms | 12.16 ms | 1.00 | 0.07 | 10.12 KB | 1.00 | | ZipFileCreateFromDirectory | After
(class) | 11.59 ms | 0.535 ms | 0.572 ms | 11.41 ms | 11.00 ms | 13.05 ms | 1.04 | 0.07 | 10.3 KB | 1.02 | I used the benchmarks that I am proposing in this PR https://github.com/dotnet/performance/pull/4764 cc @edwardneal you might be interested in this change.

### Description

I did run into a slightly funky issue in that adding to `functions.rst` for the new `GetActiveWindow()` method has no effect here. Instead, because that method is a *pure python* method, it gets its documentation differently. I punted on this and just added verbiage as a raw doc string to the pure python implementation.

I noticed I did this on the now stagnant `3.4RC`. I will cherry-pick to develop after that and when I do, I will update release notes as well, ok?

author: cosoco
body:
I don't understand why the strings of the `glob_prefs` are initialised with the default values using the long `switch ... case` statement (from line 172) with the default values instead of using the compact `jp_pref_init(...)` function. In addition, it looks much more organised and clearer if strings are defined directly in the definition of the `glob_prefs` array.

It should also run faster as it saves from layawaying through several switch cases.
It may also help to avoid issue #53 , because several `svalue` fields of `glob_prefs` stay `NULL` instead of being initialized to `""` and `svalue_size` fields stay `0` instead `1`. While developing my [JPilotMediaPlugin](https://github.com/CoSoCo/JPilotMediaPlugin/blob/main/media.c) (see from line 68) I often have seen such `SIGCHLD` crashes while reading or writing the prefs before I properly initialized (line 965) those fields.

And last, but not least, since` strdup()` allocates heap memory, isn't it also a bug that it is not freed anywhere, which is what the `jp_free_prefs()` function was intended for. This may also help to avoid issue #53 .

body:
## Description
This PR addresses the issue where the CreatePR tool fails on repositories that don't support draft PRs.

## Changes
- Modified the `create_pull` method in `GitRepoClient` to catch the specific error related to draft PRs not being supported
- Added a fallback mechanism to retry the PR creation without the draft flag when this error occurs
- Added appropriate logging to track when this fallback is used

## Testing
This change should allow the CreatePR tool to work on all repositories, regardless of whether they support draft PRs or not.

Fixes CG-11610

Watch for infinite loops... :| its super easy for glamourer to loop you, but also really easy to "stop" the loop but just disabling the rules 1 by one. No different than spam changing outfits. Doesn't actually get caught in an infinite loop in code. Only when you a loop is finished, it updates your looks (changing your race), then the rules get updated etc etc....

There's an extra window pop-up warning of this, and requiring users to "yield right to complain"

author: brennan-macaig
body:
This pull request modifies the AutoAlignment features to use JoystickApproach as opposed to using PathFinder or PathPlaner.

JoystickApproach is a command which when given a pose2d, will approach the given pose by using a PID controller to align laterally and angularly, and will allow the driver to use the joysticks Y component to travel closer to the pose (robot relative, not field relative). This means that the driver controls the speed at which they approach the pose, but the alignment of the robot and heading are locked to the target pose.

Additionally, this PR changes FieldConstants to use the FieldConstants file given by MechanicalAdvantage, which does not hardcode reef poses and instead fills them from a first given face by rotating them around the field origin and center of the reef.
